Vandalism & break-ins

Vandalism and Break-In Restoration

A keyed door, a smashed window, spray paint, a glovebox dumped on the floor. Our job is to get the vehicle back to looking and smelling like yours, and to document everything so your claim goes smoothly.

What we do after a break-in or vandalism

  • Keyed and scratched paint: we measure how deep the scratch goes. Scratches in the clear coat can usually be polished out; scratches to primer or metal need paint, and we will tell you which is which.
  • Spray paint, markers, egg and adhesive: removed from paint, glass and trim with methods that lift the contaminant rather than grind the finish.
  • Broken glass cleanup: tempered glass shatters into thousands of pieces that travel into seat tracks, vents and under carpet. We remove them so nobody finds one later.
  • Interior restoration: dumped contents, spills, footprints, cut seats and torn panels. Shampoo, extraction, upholstery repair and odor treatment as needed.
  • Documentation: dated photos of every damaged area and an itemized estimate you can submit with a police report and claim.

What to do right now

  1. If anything was stolen, file a police report. Insurers usually ask for the report number on a vandalism or theft claim.
  2. Photograph everything before you clean anything, including the ground around the vehicle and any note or tag left behind.
  3. Cover a broken window with plastic and tape to keep rain out. Do not vacuum glass with a household vacuum; it will not survive.
  4. Send us the photos. We will tell you what can be restored and what needs a body or glass shop.

What we do not do

  • Panel replacement, dent repair and repainting are body-shop work. We will say so plainly if that is what your vehicle needs.
  • Glass replacement itself is done by a glass shop; see our broken glass and interior cleanup page for how that fits together.

Deep scratches: if you can catch a fingernail in the scratch, it is probably through the clear coat. We can still improve how it looks, but we will not promise it disappears.

Vandalism and your insurance

Vandalism is typically a comprehensive claim, not collision, and comprehensive claims often do not affect your rate the way an at-fault accident does, but that depends on your policy and your insurer. If the repair is close to your deductible, many people simply pay out of pocket. Coverage, and what your deductible is, are always your insurance company’s decision, never ours.

We don’t bill your insurance company for you: you receive a written, itemized estimate and photos you can submit with your claim, and we work from the estimate once you decide to proceed.

Questions people ask

Can keyed paint be fixed without repainting?

Often, if the scratch is only in the clear coat. We polish the area and blend it. If the key went through to primer or metal, the panel needs paint, which is body-shop work; we will tell you which case you have before any work starts.

Do I need a police report?

For a vandalism or theft claim your insurer will usually want a report number. For the estimate itself we do not need it, so send photos first and file the report in parallel.

Will a vandalism claim raise my rates?

Vandalism is normally a comprehensive claim, which many insurers treat differently from an at-fault accident, but it varies by company and policy. Ask your agent. We can give you the estimate first so you can decide whether to claim.

Can you get all the glass out of the car?

Yes. Tempered glass spreads into seat tracks, door cavities, vents and under the carpet, so we remove seats and trim where needed and vacuum, brush and blow every cavity out.

How long does it take?

It depends on the damage. Light scratch polishing and glass cleanup is often a same-day or next-day job once scheduled; interior repairs take longer. We give you a time estimate with the written estimate.
